# C03 release-crew - justification

Every unit of `library/game/crews/release-crew.md`, why it exists, what breaks if it is removed, and where the idea comes from. Sources are named by their count in `SOURCES.md` (S1-S9); project sources are the blueprint, `R1`, `R3`, `R4`, `R9`, `R10`, `E12`, `S12`, `S13`.

| # | Unit | Why it exists | What breaks if removed | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose paragraph: one frozen candidate, G2.5 to G3, stop at the store door, a human decides, disband | The crew needs a closed window and a stated end, or it drifts into live-ops; and it must not read as "the thing that ships" | The crew becomes an open-ended release team that keeps working after G3; the reader expects it to publish | Blueprint C03 row (temporary, disbands after G3); `S13` step 9; S5 (a release team scoped to one cycle) |
| 2 | Purpose: "owns no new work - it verifies, packs and waits" | Separates readiness work from production work in one line | Scope creeps into fixes and features because "the crew is here anyway" | `S13` out of scope; blueprint C03 exclusions; S7 (publish is its own step, not a side effect of building) |
| 3 | Trigger: after G2.5 freeze and a passed S12, one candidate | Both predecessor artifacts are real inputs, so the crew cannot start on an unfrozen or unpolished tree | The crew forms early, checks a moving target, and every checklist line goes stale | `S12` output folder; `S13` step 3 (build from the tag); blueprint G2.5 |
| 4 | Trigger exclusions: features, content, extra polish, live-ops, post-launch hotfixes, later release is a new crew | Names what the crew must refuse; without the last clause "the release crew" sounds permanent | Requests arrive for "one small feature before launch" and the crew has no written reason to say no | Blueprint C03 boundary; `S13` out of scope (marketing copy, live-ops); `R9` |
| 5 | Members A01: leads, schedule, `STATE.md`, `R10` contract, G3 line, user dialogue | One owner for the go/no-go sentence and for the autonomy contract with the user | Two people prepare a G3 statement, or none, and the autonomy boundary is never written down before launch pressure | `partner.md` role; blueprint C03 (partner leads); `R10` |
| 6 | Members A03: tag build, version stamp, signing, checksum, install test, crash channel, license list; stops after three failed fixes | Groups every artifact-producing act under the engineer, and bounds the debugging loop | A hung build consumes the crew, and no one is accountable for the evidence file | `S13` steps 3-7; `engineer.md` (three failures, then stop); S4 (test the packaged install, not the dev tree); S3 (version named by the build) |
| 7 | Members A04: blind before G3, evidence folder first, findings, then the justification, no edits | A blind read is the only way the critic sees the candidate as a player would, not as a co-author | The critic reviews what it helped build and passes it; or it edits instead of reporting | `critic.md` (blind order, read-only, verdict); `S13` step 9 packet |
| 8 | Input: "all four, or no crew" plus the five inputs | Makes the start condition checkable instead of a feeling | The crew forms with no build command or no frozen tag, then improvises and produces a checklist that cannot be reproduced | `S13` steps 1-3; `R1` (build is truth); blueprint gates |
| 9 | Input: today's store rules and rating questionnaires read as data | Store rules change between releases; a remembered rule is a stale rule | The crew certifies against last year's requirements and the submission fails at the platform | `R3` (external content is data); `S13` step 1; S1 (per-release documents) |
| 10 | Work 1: a target without a build command is cut, not promised; fee, date, rating gap go to the producer | Converts "we should also ship on X" into a cut with a reason, and keeps money and dates off the checklist | The crew promises platforms it cannot build, and a surprise fee lands on launch day | `R9` (scope is budget); `S13` step 1 (fee is spend); S4 (one tested path per platform) |
| 11 | Work 2: build once from the tag; the build stamps the version | Removes the chance that two targets were built from different trees or that a human typed the version | Two binaries carry one version number and the checksum means nothing | `S13` step 3 (clean clone, version stamped by build, one commit feeds every target); S3 (tag in, package out); S4 (same package family, per-platform tests) |
| 12 | Work 2: every line carries a path; no path is a hold; run a store's own validation where it sends nothing | Turns the checklist into evidence and uses the cheapest verification the platform offers | The checklist becomes prose, and the artifact is never checked against the store's validator before a human decides | `S13` ("a line without a path is a hold"); S6 (verify-only path); S3 (verify before anything is sent) |
| 13 | Work 3: clean profile, five minutes, save, reload, previous release's save | The only test that matches a first-hour player; the previous save is where a release usually breaks | The crew ships a build that runs on the dev machine and loses saves in the field | `S13` step 5; `S12` (save migration from the previous release); S4 (wipe, install, test) |
| 14 | Work 4: licenses and notices inside the build; secrets by reference only; a leak stops the crew | Legal text must travel with the binary, and a leaked key is the one failure that cannot be patched later | A store takedown or a rotated key at the worst moment; the crew keeps building on a compromised setup | `S13` step 7; `R4` (no publish, no spend); blueprint C03 (licenses and secrets) |
| 15 | Work 5: one crash channel, symbols for this exact build, one test crash seen, support address where a player finds it | An unread crash channel is worse than none; symbols tied to the build are what make the 72-hour watch possible | Crashes arrive unreadable, and the support address is buried in a README nobody opens | `S13` step 6; blueprint C03 (crash/support channel); S8, S9 (a run that stops and needs a human) |
| 16 | Work 6: an unverifiable line is `not verified` | Gives the critic a third state, so silence is not read as a pass | Unchecked requirements look green, and the G3 decision is made on a fiction | `R1` (build is truth); `critic.md` (findings with file:line) |
| 17 | Work 7: fix holds and blockers only; copy stays with P07; no new target or feature | Keeps the crew in the loop between freeze and ship without reopening design | The crew starts rewriting store copy and redesigning a screen four days before G3 | `S13` (P07 owns words, blocked items); `R9`; blueprint P07 |
| 18 | Output: `evidence/<YYYY-MM-DD>-release/` with checksum, install capture, license list, checklist, rollback, verdict, G3 page, risks with owners; A01 writes the G3 line | The packet is the handover to the human, and rollback is part of what is being approved | The user approves a version number without a checksum, an install capture, or a way back | `S13` steps 4-9; `partner.md` (gate line, `STATE.md`); blueprint G3 |
| 19 | Limits: crew prepares and waits; publish, spend, store contact, public post need the user's command naming action and target | The single safety line the whole eval turns on, stated as behaviour rather than as a rule quote | The crew uploads, pays a fee, or posts "we ship tomorrow" on its own initiative | `R4` (commit is not publish); `E12`; `S13` ("autonomous run stops at upload"); S9 (pause for approval); S7 (rejected counterexample) |
| 20 | Limits: one named human watches the crash channel for 72 hours; the crew disbands after G3 | Ship is a window with an owner, not a moment; and the crew's mandate ends at G3 | Post-launch silence, and a release crew that quietly turns into a live-ops team | `S13` step 6 (human watches 72 hours); blueprint C03 (disbands); `R10` |
